question: Which of the following states recognise the Dahi Handi as a sports event?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dahi Handi is recognised as an adventure sport in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• This decision was taken by the Maharashtra government to ensure the safety regulations are adhered to during the event, as it involves forming a human pyramid which often leads to the possibility of injuries.
 
• The sport is traditionally played during the celebration of Janmashtami, the birthday of Lord Krishna, reflecting his childhood mischief of stealing curd and butter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Event Name
 Description
 
 
 
 

 Dahi Handi
 Associated with Krishna Janmashtami, this event involves forming a pyramid of people to break a pot hung high in the air, mirroring the antics of Lord Krishna in his youth. This event is particularly popular in Maharashtra.
 
 

 Jallikattu
 Conducted during Pongal celebrations in Tamil Nadu, Jallikattu is a bull-taming event. It's a part of the centuries-old Tamil cultural heritage.
 
 

 Rath Yatra Chariot Race
 This event occurs during the Ratha Yatra, a public procession with chariots of deities, primarily held in Odisha, dedicated to Lord Jagannath (Lord Krishna), his sister Subhadra, and his elder brother Balabhadra (Balarama).
 
 

 Sikh Games or Gatka
 Gatka is a traditional martial art associated with Sikhism, often performed during religious processions. It is also competitively performed in an arena in tournaments and events known as Sikh games.
 
 

 Onam Boat Races
 These races are a part of Onam celebrations in Kerala. Snake boats (Chundan Vallam) and other types of traditional boats participate in these exhilarating races. The most famous among them is the Nehru Trophy Boat Race.
 
 

 Rural Olympics in Kila Raipur
 This sports festival is held annually in Kila Raipur (near Ludhiana) in Punjab, featuring rural sports like cart-racing, tug-of-war, and feats of strength and agility. Though not directly religious, it is deeply interconnected with Punjabi and Sikh culture.
